title: Inquest eyed into OPP's fatal shooting at rural trailer park
article: The coroner for Eastern Ontario is planning to call an inquest into the death of a 20-year-old Elgin man shot in November 2005 by an OPP officer who was cleared of wrongdoing by the province's police watchdog last December.
Jason Steacy died after an officer, believing the young man had a gun, shot him in the chest on the night of Nov. 4, 2005, at a trailer park in Elgin, about 50 km north of Kingston.

A lengthy investigation by the Ontario Special Investigations Unit concluded Steacy didn't have a gun in his hand, but instead a black computer mouse. But the SIU concluded the officer who pulled the trigger had "good reason" to fear Steacy might be armed when they entered a trailer to arrest him.

According to the SIU investigation, two OPP officers were called to the trailer park to deal with an irate and intoxicated Steacy, whose police record was flagged for violence and mental instability. The officers learned Steacy had just stabbed a man in the neck with a knife and fled the scene.

Police found Steacy in a trailer talking on a telephone and two officers went to arrest him. Steacy was sitting in front of a computer when he turned toward the officers, who saw the black object in his other hand and commanded him to "put it down."
An officer fired when Steacy continued to turn toward police, according to the SIU, which concluded that forensic evidence backed the evidence provided by the officers.
SIU director James Cornish concluded the officer "reasonably feared for his life and safety and for that of his fellow officer and was justified in using deadly force."
The coroner's office yesterday confirmed it will call a "mandatory" death inquest, which has not yest been scheduled.
The purpose of a coroner's inquest is to determine the circumstances surrounding a death. An inquest jury can make recommendations in an effort to prevent similar deaths.
